pr_title: sql: Alter Column Type Using Expression
pr_body:
sql: support alter column type using expression

Fixes #47706

Release note (sql change): Support ALTER COLUMN TYPE ... USING EXPRESSION
to allow users to optionally provide an expression to convert a column to a new type.
pr_comments: This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/49452)
Would like some comments on the use of crdb_internal.force_error() in the old column's computed expression to disable writes into the old column.

I also fixed a small bug with the replaceVars logic, it didn't explicitly forbid column references from other tables when checking expressions. Because of this, there's a small bug on master where you can refer to columns in other tables when creating computed columns, check exprs, etc.
The column will get normalized and it will refer to the column in the current table. Heres an example.

```
root@127.0.0.1:54117/movr> create table t(x int, y int);
CREATE TABLE

Time: 2.383ms

root@127.0.0.1:54117/movr> create table t2(x int);
CREATE TABLE

Time: 3.252ms

root@127.0.0.1:54117/movr> insert into t2 values (1);
INSERT 1

Time: 2.512ms

root@127.0.0.1:54117/movr> alter table t add column z int as (t2.x + 1) stored;
root@127.0.0.1:54117/movr> show create table t;
  table_name |             create_statement
-------------+--------------------------------------------
  t          | CREATE TABLE t (
             |     x INT8 NULL,
             |     y INT8 NULL,
             |     z INT8 NULL AS (x + 1:::INT8) STORED,
             |     FAMILY "primary" (x, y, rowid, z)
             | )
root@127.0.0.1:54117/movr> select * from t;
  x | y | z
----+---+----
(0 rows)
```
I'm surprised that this bug was on master -- nice find! Did it basically just check if i had `<othertable>.col` that `col` was a valid column in the target table?

> I'm surprised that this bug was on master -- nice find! Did it basically just check if i had `<othertable>.col` that `col` was a valid column in the target table?

Yeah that's exactly it.

> > _[Reviewable](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/49452)_ status: :shipit: complete! 0 of 0 LGTMs obtained (waiting on @jordanlewis, @RichardJCai, @rohany, and @solongordon)
> 
> _[pkg/sql/schemaexpr/column.go, line 243 at r4](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/49452#-M9PACcOC_BWAHLQxvNI:-M9P_bnhDwA0UGwJmsXr:bh01npd) ([raw file](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/ad9bd592c76d38073b6e4b77cbb5fc054482a70b/pkg/sql/schemaexpr/column.go#L243)):_
> 
> Previously, RichardJCai (Richard Cai) wrote…
> ColumnItems contain a `UnresolvedObjectName`, which you can access the database, schema, and table from

Wait yeah you're right it I thought it only contained the actual name of the table at first glance.

I wonder if it would be alright to disable the use of database references (and schema? probably not for schema even thought we don't really support user defined schemas right now) identified table names completely.

We don't have the database/schema name handy when we do this check, would have to go and retrieve the DatabaseDescriptor using the TableDescriptors ID.

The one caveat being Postgres does support providing these identifiers for views but not for check constraints or computed columns.

You get this error when trying to reference cross database columns in postgres
```
d=# create table t3(x int generated always as (postgres.t.x > 0) stored);
ERROR:  missing FROM-clause entry for table "t"
LINE 1: create table t3(x int generated always as (postgres.t.x > 0)...
```

@rohany @solongordon
That seems reasonable to me -- If the unresolved name has > 1 part, then it's going to be possibly referencing not the current table, so i think its fine to just block that use.

> That seems reasonable to me -- If the unresolved name has > 1 part, then it's going to be possibly referencing not the current table, so i think its fine to just block that use.

Pushed a patch to disallow specifying columns and db names when referring to columns.

Tagging @mgartner since this changes some of the partial index logic. For context, I changed the replaceVars logic in schemaexpr/column.go to no longer allow columns qualified with database and schema names, there are some tests that changed because of this as well. 

I think this should be okay since database/schema names are normalized, if we allow them without checking if the database/schema names match, we allow references to other db/schema names which end up getting normalized to only the column name which is definitely a bug. 

The one case where this might matter is if a user actually wants to provide the db/schema name, where it's actually the db/schema for the table but this seems unnecessary. I'm not 100% sure though.

PTAL and let me know if this is okay.

> --------+---------+-----------+----------+---------

> Indexes:
>     "idx" btree (i) WHERE i = 1
> ```
> 
> You mentioned that database/schema names are normalized and I agree that if they are normalized before checking if they are valid, that would lead to a bug. But I don't see any current bug in CRDB:
> 
> ```
> root@127.0.0.1:52830/defaultdb> set experimental_partial_indexes=on;
> SET

> ERROR: no data source matches prefix: badschema.t
> SQLSTATE: 42P01
> ```

> Am I missing something?
> 
> _[pkg/sql/schemaexpr/partial_index_test.go, line 83 at r5](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/49452#-M9Q82wMrBQMEMTkV3rJ-r5-83:-M9VCMxC6jAS32vhqGPY:bowrvzm) ([raw file](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/9b72dd067d55817ace82d6258986e3619f6c8205/pkg/sql/schemaexpr/partial_index_test.go#L83)):_

> Yes. See my other comment.

Yeah I think we probably can't outright disable it. It seems to be okay in your case (I think it's because the optimizer will handle the name resolution correctly in the create statement). However it seems for some ALTER statements we don't correctly check, ie for computed expressions. Also it only happens when there are two tables that have a column that share the same column name.

I've created a separate issue for this here and will not change the behaviour for this in this pr. https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/50069
Any more comments on this before merging?

issue_context.title: sql: ALTER COLUMN TYPE USING EXPRESSION not supported
issue_context.body:
Currently, doing an ALTER TABLE ... ALTER COLUMN ... [SET] TYPE USING <EXPR>  is not supported.

To support this - need to disable writes into the new column while the old column still exists and is a computed column of the new one.

This stems from the problem of having two possible TableDescriptor versions once the column with the new type is swapped with the column of the old type - we need to ensure the old column is also written to in case a read happens from the old TableDescriptor. If an expression was used to generate the new column, we cannot invert the expression to use as a computed expression for the old column. Thus we have have to disable writes until the old column is dropped.

Epic CRDB-2450

Jira issue: CRDB-13696
comments: What does this do? You should add some details, and label the issue according to convention as well.

review_comments: Does anything weird happen here by setting the name of the column in the expression here -- I know we pick new names for columns in the mutation.

I think this is the correct behaviour since both the computed expressions should be based on the name of the current column. When backfilling the old column, we use the current column and then the "inverse" expression is used after the swap so the new column will now be named as the original column name.
